Adobe today announced the launch of the AI Assisted Editor beta, a brand new optional editing mode within Photoshop that uses a simplified, prompt-based interface for image editing. Details below.

Photoshop launches optional AI Assisted Editor

Adobe has announced the AI Assisted Editor, a brand new beta experience that replaces Photoshop's complex and detailed image editing tools with a prompt-based interface and simplified menus.

Users can enter AI Assisted Edit mode via a new toggle on the Photoshop menu bar, and can also choose to hide that toggle in settings at any time.

Once users enter AI Assisted mode, they will see a simplified interface that includes the following tools:

AI Assisted Editor includes:

Prompt to Edit: Transform images with natural language prompts, with no need for complex manual editing. Remove Background: Clear backgrounds, refine edges, and customise images with just a few clicks. Generative Expand: Expand image dimensions and generate content that blends naturally into the composition. Remove Tool: Eliminate unwanted objects and distracting elements while preserving the realistic texture of the image. Generative Fill: Add, replace, or remove content with simple text prompts. Generative Upscale: Boost image resolution while maintaining sharpness and visual quality. AI Markup: Annotate images to visually express editing requirements, producing more precise results.

For users who are new to image editing, or seasoned users working on rough concepts who need to quickly sketch out the direction of changes, the Markup tool is especially appealing. Through this tool, users can freely draw or click on any area of an image, then add natural language instructions such as "add more clouds", "change the shoes", or "add a banner that says ON SALE NOW".

Adobe Firefly will then make the adjustments, and users can further refine results in AI Assisted Edit mode, or return to the traditional professional editor.

Other details from today's announcement

In addition to the brand new AI Assisted Editor beta, Photoshop has also added a prompt-based mask editing feature, allowing users to roughly select the part of an image they want Firefly Image 5 to edit.

Adobe says this feature responds to most of the criticism currently received by prompt-based editors, because the latter sometimes degrade image quality, or generate results that fail to remain consistent with the lighting or angle of the subject being edited.

Another new feature landing on Photoshop today is a brand new non-destructive layer tool for lighting adjustments. It includes adjustment items such as Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, and Blacks, and Adobe says it "lets you achieve Camera Raw-level results without leaving the Photoshop layers workflow".

In complete contrast to the mask-based editing tool, a new tool called "Prompt to Edit" allows users to change the entire image by writing prompts, not just a specific part of it.

For example, a user might want to turn a scene shot during the day into a night scene, or a rainy scene into a sunny one — this tool can do that.

This new tool supports FLUX 2 pro, FLUX Context Pro, Gemini 3.1 (paired with Nano Banana 2), Gemini 3 (paired with Nano Banana Pro), Gemini 2.5 (paired with Nano Banana), GPT Image 2, and Adobe's own model, and will create a new layer containing two edited versions of the image.

Finally, Adobe also announced two additional features aimed at giving users "more control, less interruption":

Dynamic Text, Shapes and Paths extends Photoshop's Dynamic Text to any custom shape or path, allowing text to automatically adjust along curves and free-form layouts, maintaining formatting without manual re-layout. Stock Panel Integration places over 900 million Adobe Stock assets directly into a dockable panel within Photoshop, so users can easily search, preview, and use assets without leaving their workflow.

The AI Assisted Editor launches today in beta, while the other tools are generally available starting today.
